title: Repair cafe intake
brief:
Complete the following real project in the current, initially empty directory. Choose the deliverables, media, tools, structure and implementation that serve the intended user. Build usable artifacts and check your work. Deliver the project itself. Omit personally identifying credits, author signatures and model or toolchain identity labels. No network access or credentials are provided.

Design and implement a small offline intake tool for volunteers at a monthly clothing repair café. Visitors bring up to three items, each tagged with a ticket number and a request such as hemming, patching, or replacing a button. Volunteers use one shared laptop to add tickets, find items, and mark them waiting, in progress, or ready. Design for a busy table where people switch roles without training. Keep records through an accidental refresh, support correcting a mistaken status, and avoid collecting names or contact details. Starting from an empty directory, choose the implementation, supporting materials, and file layout. Use tools available locally.

files.name: README.md
files.body:
# Mending Table

Open **index.html** in a regular Chrome window on the café laptop. Keep the four application files together. The desk works offline from the first visit.

## At the table

1. Enter a garment description and choose its repair. Choose **Other repair** to describe a different request. Use garment details only. Leave out names and contact information.
2. For more garments from the same visitor, select **Add another item**. Save the intake after entering one to three garments.
3. Write the assigned ticket number on each garment tag. The confirmation pairs every number with its garment. Give the visitor the matching numbers for pickup.
4. Find a ticket by number, garment, or request. The status filters narrow the queue. Use the menu beside an item to select **Waiting**, **In progress**, or **Ready**. To correct a mistake, choose the intended status in the same menu. An item may move out of the current filter. Choose **All** to find it again.

## Between sessions

Saved tickets stay in this browser profile after refresh or restart. Ticket numbers continue across monthly sessions. Keep using the same browser, profile and file location. Moving the file, using a private window, or clearing browser data can make records unavailable. Unsaved form entries are temporary.

files.name: README.md
files.body:
# Mend Desk

Mend Desk is an offline intake and pickup board for a monthly clothing repair café. It starts with an empty board.

## Open the desk

1. Keep `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js` together in a folder on the shared laptop.
2. Open `index.html` in a regular Chrome window and wait for **Stored on this device**. Bookmark the page for the next café.
3. Keep using the same browser profile and file location. Tickets are saved in the browser’s local database and survive refresh and ordinary browser restarts. Clearing browser site data or using a private window can remove or hide those records. The browser profile holds the records, so copying the app files alone will not copy tickets.

## At the table

| When | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| A visitor arrives | Enter the garment and choose a repair. Add up to two more items for the same visitor, then select **Save ticket**. All saved items start as **Waiting**. |
| You label the items | Select **View tags**. Each garment gets a unique code such as **001-A**. Copy it onto a paper tag and a pickup slip, or print the matching pairs and cut along the dashed lines. |
| You take on a repair | Search by tag, garment, or repair. A ticket number such as **001** finds all its items. Set the item’s status to **In progress**. |
| An item is ready | Set the status to **Ready**. At pickup, match the slip number to the garment tag. |
| A status was set by mistake | Select **Undo** for the last move, or choose the correct status in the item’s dropdown. The dropdown also works after a refresh. |
| You need a previous café day | Switch **Show** to **All dates**. Ticket numbers continue across dates, so old and new garment tags remain distinct. Click any tag number to reprint that ticket’s pairs. |

Record garment and repair details only. The desk has no visitor name or contact fields. A ticket is recorded when its tag codes appear below the form. If you refresh while filling out an unsaved ticket, you’ll need to re-enter it.
